title: Residual Networks
interviewAnswer: Residual connections learn a change relative to the input and create shorter gradient paths, making very deep networks easier to optimize.
why: Residual networks are foundational because skip connections changed the trainability of very deep models and appear throughout modern architectures.
intuition: Instead of forcing a block to learn a full transformation H(x), learn a residual F(x)=H(x)-x and add the input back: y=x+F(x).
deepDive: Identity shortcuts create short gradient paths and make it easier for a block to behave like identity if extra depth is unnecessary. When shapes differ, projection shortcuts can align dimensions. Residual connections do not eliminate all optimization issues but significantly improve signal/gradient propagation and are also used in transformers and diffusion U-Nets.
workedExample: If a residual branch initially outputs near zero, the block behaves approximately like identity, so adding depth does not necessarily destroy an already useful representation.
commonMistakes: Saying ResNet solves vanishing gradients completely.
Adding tensors with incompatible shapes without projection.
Confusing residual connections with DenseNet concatenation.
production: Residual backbones are mature/efficient; inference optimization often benefits from standard kernels and well-supported architectures.
